backlogged.summary: The fragment rule applies to every string in the recorded files, not only to cut command output. Any string of 8 or more characters that starts with a suffix of a non-allowlisted env value, or ends with a prefix of one, is replaced by '[redacted]'. Examples are a path fragment or a title-like string. This matches SPEC SR-9 but can garble unrelated short strings when env values are path-like.

`harness verify` (lib/commands/verify.mjs) still calls verify() without a redactor. Its terminal output is not one of the five record paths, so it stays unredacted. It would matter if that output were ever piped into a record.

exec.mjs caps the captured output to its tail before verify redacts it. A cut at that earlier cap is only handled by the leading-fragment rule, which needs 8 or more characters of the value. That is acceptable under SR-9 but is not tested.

The metrics redaction keeps only feature, step, started_at and ended_at. The role, adapter, model and outcome strings are also passed through the redactor, which is harmless but slightly wider than needed.

The redaction of adapter-error text ('crashed [redacted]') is tested only with a leading fragment of the secret that keeps its ending. The trailing-fragment path through metrics, backlog and verdict is covered only by redactor unit tests, not by end-to-end fixtures.

Adapter error detail is cut by tail() in lib/adapters/common.mjs:175 and then placed in the middle of a string, e.g. run.mjs:1031 `builder ${error} (${detail})` or 966. A fragment of a secret at the cut ends up mid-string, so the edge-fragment rule never sees it and it can reach the state file, report or backlog. SPEC SR-9 explicitly puts mid-string fragments out of scope. Consider redacting `detail` before it is embedded, or redacting in the adapter before tail().

A string that is entirely an inner slice of a secret (both edges cut, e.g. S.slice(3,30)) is not redacted, because it is neither a prefix nor a suffix of the value. The current verify paths do not produce this, since they redact before cutting. SR-9 documents it as out of scope.

trailingFragment only matches when the string ends exactly on the prefix. A prefix fragment followed by a trailing newline or whitespace ('head sk-abcdefgh\n') is not redacted, while leadingFragment does handle 'fragment...\r\n' at the start. There is no current path that produces this, because start-cuts happen after redaction.

evalAndRecord builds its metrics redactor from process.env, while evaluate() redacts the verdict with its own `env` parameter. The two coincide in production, but a caller that passes a custom env gets metrics redacted against a different value set.
